root_cause.text: In the TUN driver’s tun_put_user(), an on-stack struct virtio_net_hdr_v1_hash_tunnel was copied to userspace without being fully initialized, because tun_vnet_hdr_tnl_from_skb() only fills the base 10-byte virtio_net_hdr for non-tunnel skbs while userspace-controlled vnet header size could request all 24 bytes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `memset(&hdr, 0, sizeof(hdr));` immediately after declaring `struct virtio_net_hdr_v1_hash_tunnel hdr;`, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that for non-tunnel packets only the first 10 bytes were initialized, bytes 10..23 remained stack garbage, and `TUNSETVNETHDRSZ` allowed `__tun_vnet_hdr_put()` to copy all 24 bytes to userspace.

intent_record.how: This initializes the entire header structure to zero before it is populated, preventing uninitialized stack data from remaining in any fields or padding that tun_vnet_hdr_tnl_from_skb() does not explicitly set and ensuring deterministic header contents at runtime.

candidates.rationale: This stack-allocated header is left uninitialized. Later code copies this struct to userspace, and for non-tunnel skbs only the base virtio header fields are filled, so the remaining bytes can leak uninitialized stack data.

This call populates the header, but per the root cause it only initializes the base 10-byte virtio_net_hdr for non-tunnel skbs, leaving the rest of the larger userspace-requested header uninitialized.

vuln_statements.explanation: This stack-allocated header is not initialized before being passed to header-population logic and then copied to userspace. For non-tunnel skbs, only the base virtio_net_hdr portion is filled, so the remaining bytes in this larger structure can contain uninitialized stack data and be leaked.

This call is the incomplete initializer: for non-tunnel skbs it fills only the base 10-byte virtio header fields, while userspace may request copying the full 24-byte virtio_net_hdr_v1_hash_tunnel, causing uninitialized bytes in hdr to remain and later reach userspace.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact vulnerable path in tun_put_user(). In this commit, tun_put_user() declares an on-stack extended header with `struct virtio_net_hdr_v1_hash_tunnel hdr;` and then calls `ret = tun_vnet_hdr_tnl_from_skb(tun->flags, tun->dev, skb, &hdr);` followed by `gso = (struct virtio_net_hdr *)&hdr;` and `ret = __tun_vnet_hdr_put(vnet_hdr_sz, tun->dev->features, iter, gso);`. There is no `memset(&hdr, 0, sizeof(hdr))` or other full initialization in tun_put_user() before passing `&hdr` to userspace serialization. Per the root cause, `tun_vnet_hdr_tnl_from_skb()` may fill only the base 10-byte virtio header for non-tunnel skbs, while userspace-controlled `vnet_hdr_sz` can cause `__tun_vnet_hdr_put()` to copy the larger 24-byte extended structure. That means uninitialized stack bytes from `hdr` can be exposed. The fix is not present here because, unlike tun_get_user() in the same diff which explicitly says `Keep it easy and always zero the whole buffer` and does `memset(&hdr, 0, sizeof(hdr));`, tun_put_user() lacks any such initialization before serialization.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact changed logic in `tun_put_user()` where the vulnerable uninitialized stack-header issue would occur. In this commit, `tun_put_user()` no longer uses only `struct virtio_net_hdr gso;`. Instead it declares `struct virtio_net_hdr_v1_hash_tunnel hdr;` and passes `&hdr` to `tun_vnet_hdr_tnl_from_skb(tun->flags, tun->dev, skb, &hdr);`, then writes to userspace via `__tun_vnet_hdr_put(vnet_hdr_sz, tun->dev->features, iter, gso);`. The commit message and surrounding diff indicate the new helpers compute/validate header size against enabled offloads, and the added comment in `tun_put_user()` says: `Drop the packet if the configured header size is too small WRT the enabled offloads.` That is the fix direction for the root cause: avoid blindly copying a larger user-requested vnet header when only a smaller base header is valid. Also, elsewhere in the same diff the receive-side path explicitly zeroes the whole extended header buffer (`memset(&hdr, 0, sizeof(hdr));`) before use, showing the commit is handling the larger header structure carefully. Therefore, the vulnerable construct described in the root cause—copying an on-stack `virtio_net_hdr_v1_hash_tunnel` to userspace without full initialization while userspace can request all 24 bytes—is not present here as an unchecked raw copy pattern; instead the code uses the new tunnel-aware put helper with feature/size validation, so `has_bug=false` and `is_fixed=true`.
